events.label: birth
events.text: Born in Khara-Shibir village near Ulan-Ude, Khory Buryat.

evidence.quote: 1853 , Khara-Shibir ulus

events.text: Left home at nineteen to study at Gomang College, Drepung.

evidence.quote: He left home in 1873 at nineteen to study at the Gomang College

events.label: honour
events.text: Tsar Nicholas II gave him a monogrammed watch for services rendered.

evidence.quote: In 1896 , the Tsar , Nikolai II , gave Agvan Dorzhiev a monogrammed watch

events.text: Went to Saint Petersburg to collect subscriptions for his monastic college.

evidence.quote: In early 1898 Dorzhiev went to Saint Petersburg to collect subscriptions

events.label: audience
events.text: Presented to Tsar Nicholas II in Saint Petersburg.

evidence.quote: Dorzhiev was presented to the Tsar

events.text: Returned to Russia with six other envoys from the 13th Dalai Lama.

evidence.quote: In the spring of 1900 Dorzhiev returned to Russia with six other representatives

events.label: audience
events.text: Met the Tsar at the Livadia Palace in Crimea.

evidence.quote: They travelled through India and met the Tsar at the Livadia Palace in Crimea

events.label: visit
events.text: Visited the Ninth Panchen Lama at Tashilhunpo and received teachings.

evidence.quote: In 1901 , Thubten Chökyi Nyima , the Ninth Panchen Lama ( 1883–1937 ) , was visited by Agvan Dorzhiev

events.text: Convinced the 13th Dalai Lama to flee to Urga, Mongolia.

evidence.quote: In early 1904 Dorzhiev convinced the Dalai Lama to flee to Urga in Mongolia

events.text: Obtained Tsar's permission and built the Saint Petersburg datsan.

evidence.quote: building the Buddhist temple of Saint Petersburg in 1909
In 1909 Dorzhiev got permission from the Tsar to build a large and substantial Buddhist datsan

events.text: Met the 13th Dalai Lama at Phari Dzong and escorted him to Samding.

evidence.quote: During the summer of 1912 , he met the 13th Dalai Lama at Phari Dzong

events.label: founding
events.text: Founded the manba datsan, a medical college at Atsagat monastery.

evidence.quote: Also in 1913 , Dorzhiev founded a manba datsan , a medical college

events.label: treaty
events.text: Signed the Tibet-Mongolia Treaty with Mongolian representatives in Urga.

evidence.quote: In early 1913 , Agvan Dorzhiev and two other Tibetan representatives signed a treaty in Urga
thus making it 8th January 1913 by the Gregorian
signing the Tibet-Mongolia Treaty in 1913

events.label: conference
events.text: Led and managed a conference of Tibetan doctors in Atsagat.

evidence.quote: In August 1927 , he led and managed a conference of Tibetan doctors in Atsagat

events.label: arrest
events.text: Arrested by the NKVD during Stalin's Great Purge, charged with treason.

evidence.quote: arrested by the NKVD during Joseph Stalins Great Purge on November 13 , 1937

events.label: death
events.text: Died in prison hospital custody in Ulan-Ude, aged 85.

evidence.quote: January 29 , 1938 , Ulan-Ude
transferred from his cell to the prison hospital on January 29 , 1938

events.label: rehabilitation
events.text: Case dismissed; Dorzhiev rehabilitated for lack of evidence.

evidence.quote: until May 14 , 1990 , when the case was dismissed

undated_mentions: Mid-1880s: attained the title of Tsanit Khenpo after 15 years of study
Began the Geshey Lharampa degree (no date stated)
Served as the 13th Dalai Lama's teacher and spiritual adviser until at least the late 1910s
Went on to Paris and possibly London before returning to Lhasa (after 1898)
By the 1890s began spreading the Shambhala myth about Russia
Previously acted as roving ambassador for the Dalai Lama in Russia
Created the Vagindra script for writing the Buryat language (no date stated)
Circulated a pamphlet on the Russian Tsar and Shambhala (no date stated)
Arrested and sentenced to death after the Russian revolution, later reprieved
Saint Petersburg temple plundered and his papers destroyed after the Russian revolution
Proposed converting monasteries into collective farms (no date stated)
Advocated adding Oirat Mongol areas to Outer Mongolia (no date stated)
Co-existed with the Communists during the 1920s
Buried in a secret traditional burial place near Chelutai (no date stated)
